title: Release
core_thesis: Deployment release for physical AI is not a static software milestone, but an ongoing, cryptographically revocable lease of physical authority over mass and energy, bounded by explicit Operational Design Domains and enforced by deterministic hardware.
pedagogical_strengths: Effectively grounds abstract software deployment concepts by starkly contrasting enterprise risks (database latency) with physical AI risks (kinetic energy, force).
Moves beyond binary 'safe/unsafe' framing by introducing a rigorous, standardized trichotomy of release verdicts (unconditional, conditional, refusal).

student_friction_points.point: If foundation models cannot be certified to ASIL D, what is the exact architectural interface that allows a deterministic supervisor to safely veto deep statistical network outputs without destabilizing the system?

The text references 'non-injurious kinetic force dissipation', but needs to explicitly link this to the previously established Lyapunov stability envelopes or maximum permissible kinetic energy equations (1/2 mv^2).

The crucial concept of the 'cryptographic lease in silicon' appears suddenly in the summary. This high-level mechanism should be seeded earlier in the introductory sections to ground the abstract 'chain of evidence' language.

established_budgets_and_laws: Operational Design Domain (ODD) limits on mass, friction, velocity, and thermal dissipation.
Hardware interlock invalidation thresholds (e.g., mechanical backlash wear > 0.10°, statistical parameter drift > 3σ, maximum mechanical cycle counts N > N_max).
imported_prerequisites: The causal boundary mechanism converting computational outputs into mechanical work against physical objects (@sec-boundary-causal-boundary).
Hardware-in-the-loop stress testing and calibrated dynamometer telemetry.
The statistical opacity and unprovable nature of deep neural policies.
exported_concepts: The Claim-Argument-Evidence (CAE) safety case and Goal Structuring Notation (GSN).
The cryptographic release manifest that binds neural weights to hardware fault detectors.
The epistemic limits of empirical testing (setting up the open-world deployment challenges in Chapter 17).

surgical_edits.target_text: Determining if a physical machine should operate poses the central engineering dilemma of autonomy: *how safe is safe enough*, and how can safety be demonstrated through auditable, falsifiable claims instead of ungrounded statistical optimism?
surgical_edits.improved_text: Determining if a physical machine should operate poses the central dilemma of autonomy: *how safe is safe enough?* We must demonstrate safety not through ungrounded statistical optimism, but through auditable, falsifiable claims that form an active, revocable cryptographic lease of physical authority.

surgical_edits.improved_text: Certifying a multi-billion-parameter neural foundation model directly to ASIL D is impossible. Instead, deep statistical networks must be bounded by a deterministic, ASIL D-certified hardware envelope that physically vetoes unprovable or unsafe policy commands before they reach the actuators.

open_thematic_threads_for_part: How does the engineering discipline manage the epistemic limits of empirical safety cases when confronting the 'astronomical exposure wall' of open-world, unstructured environments?
